question: What does a holistic view of human health primarily include beyond the physical body?
explanation: Health involves a combination of physical, mental, social, and cultural factors rather than just physical well-being. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must midwives look beyond a single physical symptom when caring for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Physical symptoms are usually completely unrelated to pregnancy
options.B: Health is a unique and broad human experience affecting the whole person
options.C: Mental health has no impact on physical body functions
options.D: Hospital regulations require checking social status first

explanation: Because health encompasses many dimensions of a person's life, care must address more than just isolated physical signs. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does the World Health Organization broadly define health?

options.A: Having a normal body temperature and pulse
options.B: Just the physical absence of any body pain
options.C: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.D: The ability to work without taking a break

explanation: The WHO definition emphasizes overall well-being across physical, mental, and social domains rather than just being free of sickness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h2)

question: What makes illness different from a diagnosed medical disease?

options.A: Illness only occurs when a laboratory test is positive
options.B: Disease can never be cured, while illness always disappears quickly
options.C: Illness is a subjective feeling of being unwell, even without a formal diagnosis
options.D: Disease affects the mind while illness affects only the skin

explanation: Illness describes the personal, subjective experience of discomfort and disrupted function that a person feels inside. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h2)

question: What does the health-illness continuum represent?

options.A: A sliding scale showing health as a constantly changing state
options.B: A strict set of rules for diagnosing malaria
options.C: A laboratory test measuring blood sugar levels
options.D: A fixed medical category that never changes over time

explanation: The continuum portrays health not as a fixed point, but as a dynamic range moving between wellness and illness. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h3)

question: A pregnant woman with severe morning sickness moves toward which end of the health-illness continuum temporarily?

options.B: The illness and poor health end
options.C: The optimal wellness and peak fitness end
options.D: The complete absence of physical form

explanation: Experiencing debilitating symptoms shifts a person closer to the illness side of the continuum until relief and recovery occur. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which health model defines wellness strictly as the absence of physical signs of disease?
explanation: The clinical model focuses narrowly on the medical signs of sickness and considers a person healthy if no disease is found. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main focus of the role performance model of health?

options.A: How well a person adjusts to sudden climate changes
options.B: Having normal blood pressure and laboratory results
options.C: A person's ability to fulfill work and family duties
options.D: Achieving high spiritual and emotional happiness

explanation: This model evaluates health based on whether an individual can successfully carry out their expected daily roles in society. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an internal variable that influences health beliefs?
explanation: Internal variables arise from within the individual, such as genetics, age, and emotional maturity. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should a midwife understand the cultural background and family practices of a pregnant woman?

options.A: Hospital policies require documenting family ancestry charts
options.B: Family practices replace the need for physical examinations
options.C: External variables strongly shape health beliefs and health-seeking behaviors
options.D: Cultural background determines blood type during delivery

explanation: Culture and family background are external factors that heavily influence how a patient views illness and makes health choices. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a common impact of serious illness on a household?

options.B: Disruption of family roles and financial strain

explanation: Illness places emotional and financial pressure on a family while forcing others to take over the duties of the sick member. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important for midwives to consider the whole family when a mother is ill?

options.A: Family members are legally required to pay hospital bills
options.B: Household members always share the exact same physical disease
options.C: Illness in one member affects the daily functioning of the entire family
options.D: Midwives are trained to treat family legal issues

explanation: Because a household is interconnected, sickness in a mother changes roles and causes stress for everyone involved. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h6)
